title: Wild Bill Donovan and the original crash-retrieval protocols

tellings.quote: Chief OSS member and another CIA founder, Wild Bill Donovan, who journalist Chris Sharp notes was likely not only involved in the Magenta crash retrieval, but in setting up original protocols for UFO crash retrievals, was also a Knight of Malta.

plain: William "Wild Bill" Donovan, a top figure in the OSS (America's wartime spy service) and one of the founders of the CIA, is said to have helped recover a crashed unknown craft near Magenta in Italy. He is also said to have written the first rules for how such crash recoveries should be handled. Michels tells this from the work of a journalist named Chris Sharp, who says Donovan was "likely" involved, and Michels adds that Donovan was also a Knight of Malta, a member of an old Catholic order of knights. If true, it would mean the plan for gathering up crashed craft existed before the famous cases of the late 1940s.
